prompt: Node.java is provided and complete. Write the static methods in LinkedListOps that walk a chain of node references: length, append, toList, and a reversed that builds an entirely new chain without disturbing the original.
explanation: A linked list is nothing but objects on the heap holding references to each other; the variable `head` is just a reference to the first one, and null means "no list at all". Walking it means copying the reference into a local variable and reassigning that local to current.next, which moves the pointer without touching the objects. append returns the head because the head only changes in the empty case -- everywhere else you hand back the very same reference you were given. reversed must allocate a fresh Node per value and link each new node in front of the growing result; reusing the given nodes would rewrite their next fields and destroy the original chain.
hints: Every walk has the same shape: a Node variable starting at head, looping while it is not null, advancing to current.next each pass. Never write to current.next inside one of these loops unless you mean to change the list.
append: if head is null, the new node is the whole list, so return it. Otherwise walk with `while (last.next != null) last = last.next;` and set last.next to the new node, then return head unchanged.

reversed keeps a result reference that starts at null; for each value you walk past, build a FRESH node, point its next at the result so far, and make it the new result. Because you only ever create new nodes, the original chain is safe.
